question.text: Mr. Arjun Nair's Cat II AIF is negotiating a Series B round with 'Saraswati EdTech'. On board seats for AIF investors, the chapter notes that:

answer.text: SEBI mandates a minimum of 2 board seats per Cat II AIF investment
Cat II AIFs never receive board seats below Series C
Board seats should be allotted on a pro-rata basis based on the amount of investment, and an agreement for a seat does not itself create, appoint or bind other investors
Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (CCPS) always carry an automatic board seat

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.10 (Board composition), board seats are allotted on a pro-rata basis based on investment. An agreement between company and investor for a board seat does not in itself accomplish (i) creating the seat, (ii) appointing the investor, or (iii) binding other shareholders to vote for the appointee. Those require Shareholders' Agreement and AOA amendments. CCPS may NOT always have a board seat right. The Trap: SEBI does not mandate minimum board seats. Option C is false (Cat II routinely gets seats earlier). Option D contradicts the chapter text. Cross-Exam Context: Board-seat mechanics tested in XIX-A and in X-A/X-B for IA disclosure when advising on board-seat rights. Manager's Pro-Tip: When negotiating board seats, always add: (i) the specific director-appointment resolution, (ii) power-of-attorney from other shareholders to vote for your nominee, and (iii) AOA amendment commitment. Without all three, the 'board seat' is illusory.
